reviews.rationale: Accepted as an explicitly bounded, low-confidence selected-edition whole row. Checked the 27-word body through the 32:4 boundary, both stars, separate apparatus numbers, and the source note and uncertainty metadata. The opaque form is ከሐክቲሆሙ: the first and third Kaff forms are visually different in the same word; the third has the characteristic sixth-order left-foot/knot against headed Table I, and the following Tawe is third order. This corrects, without overwriting, my provisional source-first ከሐከቲሆሙ. The two tree forms have visibly distinct terminal Wawe VI and I, both retained, and the English preserves the doubled tree reference. I checked entry/sight, garden of righteousness, demonstrative and tree sequence, growing and there, scent and pleasant, the repeated large, beauty with singular abundance, plural glory, and the tree-of-wisdom/from-it/eating/knowing construction. Full English keeps the opaque token precisely after saw, with a disclosed English-only connector rather than a lexical substitute, and keeps scent, size, beauty and glory distinct. “I also saw” carries the opening perception forward, not a newly printed verb; “people” is nonspecific plural syntax, not an added named actor. Note a accurately distinguishes uncertainty from a print gap, the 824 doubt and 1853 contextual conjecture, and comparison-only 1851/Flemming variants; the actual edited 4Q206 snapshot places the distance wording in the bracketed restoration and is not adopted. Note b aligns scent with actual col1309 and preserves the double tree wording without an added Tree of Life. Note c is qualified appropriately: actual grammar p265 gives the eat gerund, pp285/477 show gender flexibility, and col1229 marks wisdom masculine and feminine, supporting but not proving the adjacent great-wisdom attachment. No opaque-word meaning, reconstructed source reading, chapter, release, or 32:6 guard waiver is approved.
